_schema_notes.coverage: Authoritative schema for all DID formats — DD Form 1664 (pre-2014) and free-text (post-2014 MIL-STD-963C)
_schema_notes.did_format: Set to 'dd_form_1664' or 'free_text'. Determines which fields are expected to be populated.
_schema_notes.963c_compliant: True if the DID was prepared under MIL-STD-963C (2014 or later). False for older DIDs.
_schema_notes.reserved_fields: Fields marked RESERVED are present in one format but not the other. Always include them — set to empty string or empty array when not applicable.
_schema_notes.preparation_instructions: Official MIL-STD-963C name for what was previously called 'requirements'. Contains the numbered sections of the DID. All section numbers are normalized to strictly numeric dot-notation (1, 1.1, 1.1.1). Letter-based source numbering (2.a, 3.1.b) is converted to numeric equivalents (2.1, 3.1.2).
_schema_notes.asterisk: True if the requirement number is followed by * in the source document (conditional requirement).

title: Software Assurance Case
summary: Specifies the format and content for a Software Assurance Case, a structured argument supported by evidence that justifies a software/system is acceptably assured relative to a concern such as safety or security.
use_relationship:
The Software Assurance Case is a structured argument, supported by evidence, intended to justify that the software/system is acceptably assured relative to a concern (such as safety or security) in the intended operating environment.

This Data Item Description (DID) contains the format, content, and intended use for the data product resulting from the work task described in the contract Statement of Work/Performance Work Statement.

preparation_instructions.title: Content
preparation_instructions.content: The documented evidence shall provide a convincing and valid argument that a specified set of critical claims regarding a software's/system's properties are adequately justified for a given application in a given environment. The Software Assurance Case shall be organized into the following sections:

children.title: Reference Documents
children.content: This section shall list the number, title, revision, and date of all documents referenced in this deliverable. This section shall also identify the source for all documents not available through normal Government stocking activities.

children.title: Document Management
children.content: This section shall identify the version, release date, and other relevant management and configuration control information associated with the current version of the deliverable. A change history, highlighting significant changes from version to version shall be included.

children.title: Table of Contents
children.content: This section shall index all sections, major paragraphs, subparagraphs and appendices with page numbers.

children.title: Scope
children.content: This section shall be divided into paragraphs covering system and software identification, system overview and document overview.

children.title: System and Software Identification
children.content: This section shall contain a full identification of the system and the software to which this deliverable applies, including, as applicable, identification number(s), title(s), abbreviation(s), version number(s), and release number(s).

children.title: System Overview
children.content: This section shall briefly state the purpose of the system to which this deliverable applies. It shall describe the general nature of the system and software; summarize the history of system development, operation, and maintenance; identify the project sponsor, acquirer, user, developer, and support agencies; identify current and planned operating sites; and list other relevant documents.

children.title: Document Overview
children.content: This section shall summarize the purpose and contents of the deliverable and shall describe any security or privacy considerations associated with its use.

children.title: Software Assurance Case Model
children.content: The structured assurance case model is represented as a directed graph whose nodes consist of claims, arguments, and evidence elements.

children.title: Claims and Sub-Claims
children.content: A claim is a statement asserting some characteristic, property, or behavior of the software or system that can be evaluated for truthfulness, is demonstrable, and is supported by arguments based on objective evidence. A claim may be further decomposed into subclaims, and expressed either as a positive or negative statement.

children.title: Claims and Sub-Claims
children.content: Claims and Sub-Claims should be pre-reviewed to ensure non-duplication.

children.title: Arguments
children.content: Arguments are logical propositions intended to support a claim through reasoning or logic that links evidence to a claim. An argument is the explanation of how the evidence can be interpreted as supporting a claim or sub-claim.

children.title: Evidence
children.content: Evidence is information used to support a claim. Evidence should be objective, reproducible, repeatable, and non-disputable.
